agent: Agent D — experimenter, Variant B (full stylesheet snapshot)
referenceLabel: CURRENT_SOURCE — substrate reference PNGs, 2026-08-28/29 session. NOT historical August truth.

variants.B-naive: settled dom.html verbatim + self-hosted <link> stylesheets/fonts/images, all URLs rewritten local, every <script> removed. NO computed style, NO generated classes.
variants.B-plus: B-naive + the CSSOM-only rules (styled-components v6 insertRule sheet) serialised back into the empty <style data-styled> element at its original cascade position.

headlineFinding.claim: The naive full-stylesheet snapshot FAILS, and it fails for one identifiable, generalisable reason; adding ~20 lines that serialise the CSSOM makes it near-exact.
headlineFinding.mechanism: linear.app ships styled-components v6, whose production sheet is injected with CSSOM insertRule. Its <style data-styled="active" data-styled-version="6.1.24"> node has textContent.length === 0, so documentElement.outerHTML carries the class names but none of the rules. 486 sc-* class references on /security render completely unstyled.
headlineFinding.measuredConsequence: h1 font-size 64px -> 16px, 27 font-size and 23 colour mismatches among the 150 largest elements, document height 3231 -> 3356 (desktop) and 14349 -> 15192 (mobile).
headlineFinding.fix: harvest document.styleSheets[i].cssRules for every <style> node whose textContent is empty, write it back into that same node in place (cascade position preserved). 7.2 KB on /security, 9.5 KB on /pricing.
headlineFinding.generality: Not a linear.app quirk. styled-components v6, Emotion speedy mode, JSS, Stitches and Goober all use insertRule in production. Any settled-DOM snapshotter that reads only outerHTML loses them silently — no console error, no request failure.

complementarity.note: Neither harvest path alone is sufficient.
complementarity.httpDownloadOnly: cannot see CSSOM-injected rules (0 bytes in outerHTML).
complementarity.cssomOnly: cannot read cross-origin <link> sheets — 28 sheets on /security and 30 on /pricing throw SecurityError on .cssRules because they are crossorigin="" from static.linear.app.
complementarity.conclusion: a correct capture must do BOTH: HTTP-download every linked sheet AND serialise every CSSOM-only sheet.

axes.assetIndependence: TESTED, PASS. Every non-localhost request was aborted and counted during measurement: externalRequestsAttempted = 0 on all 10 measured pairs, with 0 requestFailures, 0 consoleErrors, 0 pageErrors. 329 stylesheets, 8 font files and 15 images self-hosted (10 MB total). Zero @import statements anywhere, so no chain to follow. axes.interactionCompatibility: TESTED, SPLIT. CSS-driven states are fully alive: hovering 7 header elements repaints 53-60% of their pixels (nav anchors, Sign up button), from 381 :hover and 63 :focus selectors and 76 @keyframes that all ship self-hosted. JS-driven states are dead: the /pricing monthly-yearly control is a real <label>+<input type=checkbox checked> but clicking it repaints 0 pixels; the mobile menu trigger exists with aria-expanded=false, has no layout box, and clicking repaints 0 pixels. 139-260 <script> tags plus 359-425 modulepreloads are removed per page. Internal links stay root-relative ('/pricing') and 404 against a bare static server until a route map is applied.
axes.runtimeSourceDependency: NONE at runtime — 0 external requests, no script executes, no origin is contacted. The dependency moved entirely to CAPTURE time, and it got stricter: you now need a live browser session on the origin that can read document.styleSheets[i].cssRules. HTTP download alone is insufficient (misses the CSSOM sheet, 7.2-9.5 KB); CSSOM reading alone is insufficient (28-30 crossorigin sheets from static.linear.app throw SecurityError on .cssRules). You must do both, in the same session.
axes.abilityToSelfHost: TESTED, PASS. Plain static files over a 25-line node http server; no framework, no build step, no Next.js. 10 MB for two routes with all three per-viewport DOMs (4.3 MB /security, 5.7 MB /pricing) — and the per-viewport DOMs are redundant, so ~7 MB in practice. Would drop onto any static host or CDN unchanged.
axes.abilityToEditContentAndTheme: TESTED, PASS with a caveat. Content: replacing the /security h1 text with Korean in the raw HTML kept font-size 64px, box 592x135.66 and document height 3231; the diff vs the un-edited build is 0.0057 and confined to the heading. Theme: one appended <style> overriding --color-bg-primary/--color-text-primary/--color-text-tertiary repainted 99.78% of pixels (body 8,9,10 -> 10,31,20; 1249 elements took the new text colour) with layout untouched — because 80.7% of colour-valued declarations on /security and 79.9% on /pricing already resolve through var(--token). CAVEAT: my first attempt, overriding only --color-accent/--color-link-primary/--color-brand-bg, moved 1 element. There is no web-recon-authored token contract, so an operator is editing the SOURCE's private token vocabulary blind. Structural edits (move a section, change a grid) mean hand-editing opaque hashes like sc-KOGVz iSOwhx and _5mGmSq_root.
axes.riskOfSourceSpecificHacks: LOW in the build code, HIGH in the artifact. The 276 lines I wrote contain zero linear.app selectors: URL rewriting from map.json, script/preload stripping, and 'serialise every <style> whose textContent is empty'. That last rule is framework-shaped, not site-shaped — styled-components v6, Emotion speedy mode, JSS, Stitches and Goober all use insertRule in production, and all fail identically and silently under the naive variant. The artifact itself, however, is 100% coupled to the source's private class hashes and its runtime nondeterminism is baked in: the CustomerMarquee is frozen at one @keyframes phase, ScrambleText is frozen mid-scramble as random glyphs ('g2uc 2tli.'), and /pricing's price ticker keeps a duplicated clipped node (206 text lines vs the source's 204). Nothing can be re-derived after a source redeploy — every hash changes and you must re-capture.
